correctness.rationale: For every finite DAG with at least two source-sink routes, its unit flow polytope is exactly the convex hull of route vectors. Directed arc precedence is a finite poset and a chain extends to a route; Dilworth yields a w-route cover from a width-w antichain. Every feasible reflection with coefficient lambda forces each center coordinate >=1/(lambda+1), and every path hits an antichain at most once; hence lambda>=w-1. Averaging the route cover gives c_e>=1/w; for any such c and every route R, wc-chi_R is a nonnegative flow of strength w-1, proving containment and characterizing all optimal centers. Positive integer flows decompose into integer route vectors, and relative-interior flows have all arc coordinates positive, so codegree=w. The exact-integer standalone verifier checks the claimed identities in 1393 small DAGs. No finite test is used as a general proof.

originality.rationale: Primary full texts on acyclic unit-flow polytopes and Gorenstein flow triangulations establish route vertices, combinatorial triangulations, and a codegree formula for specially balanced networks. value.rationale: An exact affine invariant is determined for every positive-dimensional acyclic unit-flow polytope by a maximum antichain, rather than by a high-dimensional facet optimization. The full optimal-center polytope and an integral lattice codegree are simultaneously classified, yielding polynomial-time computation. The result remains valid on graphs with multiple sources/sinks, disconnected graphs, and non-Gorenstein examples requiring overlapping route covers. These are motivated natural extensions of strength-one flow-polytope research rather than a finite table or arbitrary restriction.
